species.diagnosis: Cephalon and pygidium almost round. Glabella cylindrical, divided into three segments, frontal lobe subpentagonal; median node long, at the front of the posterior lobe; glabellar transverse furrow straight; preglabellar median furrow distinct; basal lobe triangular; Border furrow broad and deep; border narrow. species.remarks: Agnostus pisiformis is the type species of Agnostus; its ventral soft-part structures have been thoroughly studied thanks to Orsten-type exceptional preservation in Sweden.

species.classification: Order Agnostida / Suborder Agnostina / Superfamily Agnostoidea / Family Agnostidae
species.genus_etymology: micr-, Greek, small; Agnostus, a trilobite genus name.
species.species_etymology: orientalis, Latin, eastern, referring to its Chinese origin.
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield elongate-oval. Cephalon subsquare; glabella convex, subcylindrical, occupying about two-thirds of the cephalic length; glabellar frontal lobe elongate, occupying about one-third of the glabellar length; posterior segment more strongly convex, middle part with elongate median node, with a pair of short, weak glabellar lateral furrows in front of the median node; dorsal furrow deep and narrow; basal lobe triangular, relatively large; cheek relatively broad; border furrow narrow and deep; border narrow and convex raised, of uniform width. Thoracic axis broad; pleural lobes narrow, pleural furrow narrow and deep, pleural spines short and extending obliquely forward. Pygidium nearly round; pygidial axis convex, occupying about three-quarters of the pygidial length; divided into three rings, the first axial ring composed of nearly square lateral lobes; second axial ring with stout axial node; posterior axial ring large, exceeding half the length of the pygidial axis; pleural lobes relatively narrow; border furrow narrow and deep; border narrow and convex, Uniform width; With a pair of tiny posterolateral spines.
species.remarks: Typical body length about 0.2-1.2 cm.

Cephalon semicircular apart from genal spines; glabella subtrapezoidal, weakly convex, glabellar furrows effaced; occipital furrow effaced, occipital ring indistinct from the glabella; dorsal furrow faint; anterior border transversely triangular; palpebral lobes arcuate and convex; fixigenae wide in the palpebral area; librigenae wide with wide lateral borders and stout genal spines; anterior branches of facial sutures slightly divergent forward, crossing the middle of the anterior border; posterior branches extending backward and slightly outward in a gentle curve. Thorax of 8 segments, axis narrower than pleurae; pleural inner parts horizontal, of uniform width; pleural spines short. Pygidium semicircular and convex; axis long-conical with many rings; pygidial border wide; two lateral spines present in meraspid and early holaspid stages.

species.diagnosis: Cranidium transversely wide and cap-like; glabella subsquare, strongly convex, with three pairs of glabellar furrows; dorsal furrows narrow; occipital furrow straight; occipital ring enlarged medially with a small occipital node; anterior border very narrow, preglabellar field absent; palpebral lobes decreasing in size with growth; eye ridges faint; fixigenae narrow in the palpebral area, posterior border furrows wide and shallow; librigenae wide with long genal spines. Thorax of 12 segments, axis tapering; pleurae wider than the axis, pleural furrows deep; pleural spines rather long, those of segments 3 and 7 being macropleural. Pygidium semicircular apart from pleural spines; anterior margin straight; axis convex, divided into four axial rings and a long triangular terminal piece that narrows rapidly; pleural lobes wide with deep pleural furrows; a pygidial spine arising from each pleural ring, the anterior ones large and stout, followed by six pairs of triangular spines, and the last pair small.

species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield verrucose. Cranidium wide; glabella truncate-conical with four pairs of glabellar furrows, L1 inverted V-shaped; occipital ring with a median node; fixigenae strongly convex; palpebral lobes raised above the glabella; preglabellar field depressed; anterior border erect; posterior margin of fixigenae denticulate; librigenae with rather long genal spines bearing denticles. Thorax of 12 segments; axis narrower than pleurae; pleural furrows transverse, pleural spines long with denticles. Pygidial axis long-conical; border narrow with 7 pairs of spines, the first pair large and long. Since Walcott 1913 this species has long been misidentified as Blackwelderia sinensis. The main differences are:
species.remarks: the posterior margin of the cephalon bears many spines, the anterior border is narrower, the palpebral area is more elevated, the glabella has an inverted V-shaped L1, the genal and pleural spines are densely covered with small denticles, and the first pair of pygidial spines is exceptionally large.

species.species_etymology: licin-, Latin, bent upward; spinata, spiny. Referring to the upward-curving pygidial spines
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield with sparse tubercles. Anterior margin of cranidium curved forward; glabella trapezoidal with 3 pairs of shallow glabellar furrows; occipital ring with a small median node; palpebral lobes medium-sized; eye ridges distinct; anterior border con vex as a wide sharp ridge; anterior branches of facial sutures parallel or slightly divergent; librigenae with short blunt genal spines. Thorax of 10 segments; axis narrower than pleurae; pleural furrows straight, narrow and deep, pleural spines short and pointed. Pygidium subtriangular apart from spines; axis long, with four rings and a terminal piece; first pleural ring extended backward-outward into a pair of long, strongly upturned pleural spines; border furrow rather deep, border medium-wide.
species.remarks: The first complete dorsal exoskeleton of this species was discovered by Axi!, a trilobite fossil enthusiast.

species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield with dense small and sparse large tubercles. Cranidium subtrapezoidal; dorsal furrows deep; glabella strongly convex, conical to subconical with pointed-rounded front; 3 pairs of glabellar furrows; occipital furrow deep; occipital ring wide medially with a small occipital node; fixigenae narrow in the palpebral area; palpebral lobes short, eye ridges faint; librigenae narrow with short genal spines. Thorax of 13 segments; axis slightly narrower than pleurae; pleural furrows wide and deep, pleural spines short. Pygidium small, elliptical; axis with 2 axial rings and a terminal piece; border narrow.
species.remarks: The first complete dorsal exoskeleton of this species was discovered by Yadong, a trilobite enthusiast from Shandong.

species.species_etymology: mirabilis, Latin, marvellous
species.distribution: Shanxi, Shandong, North China and southern Northeast China
species.diagnosis: A small trilobite with smooth dorsal shield. Cranidium convex, subtrapezoidal, anterior margin arched forward; dorsal furrows wide and deep; glabella short and small, truncate-conical, narrowing rapidly forward with truncate front, a low median ridge on the sagittal line, 4 pairs of shallow or faint glabellar furrows; occipital ring convex, semi-elliptical, wide medially with a small occipital node at the posterior centre; anterior border furrow wide and shallow, meeting the dorsal furrows at the anterior lateral corners of the glabella; anterior border wide, widest medially, raised as a dome-like swelling; fixigenae between the two palpebral lobes medium-wide, gently convex, highest near the palpebral lobes; palpebral lobes medium-long, in the mid-posterior part opposite the glabella; eye ridges fine; librigenae narrow and long, lateral border gently convex, lateral border furrow wide and shallow, genal spines medium-length; posterior border furrow wide and deep; posterior border narrow and gently convex. Thorax probably of 10 segments; pleural furrows narrow; pleural spines absent. Pygidium semi-elliptical, with 3-4 axial rings; border narrow, border furrow indistinct.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Ruichengaspis.

species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield elongate-elliptical, smooth. Anterior border of the cranidium extends forward with a large V-shaped notch in the middle, forming an ear-like shape; border narrow; glabella long-trapezoidal, slightly constricted medially, with four pairs of pit-like glabellar furrows disconnected medially; occipital furrow narrow and shallow, occipital ring of nearly uniform width; eye ridges high and strong; fixigenae wide in the palpebral area; librigenae largely trapezoidal with straight lateral margins and short sharp genal spines. species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield smooth, with concentric terrace lines on the border. Cephalon semicircular; cranidium gently convex; anterior border flat; glabella long, broadly rounded and constricted anteriorly, preglabellar furrow distinct, a median node at the posterior part of the glabella, with four pairs of ovate faint glabellar furrows; palpebral lobes semicircular; occipital ring narrow, occipital furrow deep; anterior branches of facial sutures widening forward then smoothly curving inward, meeting at an obtuse angle; librigenae wide with genal angles rounded, without genal spines. Pygidium wide, semicircular; axis gently convex, faintly indicated, with about 8-9 rings; pleural furrows faint, articulating facets triangular; border wide.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Zhiyia.

species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield smooth, with concentric terrace lines on the border. Cephalon semicircular; in some specimens the glabellar convexity and anterior border are visible; glabellar, dorsal and occipital furrows all indistinct; palpebral lobes rather large, semicircular; anterior branches of facial sutures widening forward then smoothly curving inward, meeting at an obtuse angle; librigenae wide with rounded, spineless genal angles. Thorax of 8 segments; axis subrectangular, slightly wider than pleurae; pygidium semicircular; axis indistinct; border wide.
species.remarks: Compared with the type species Zhiyia tsinghaiensis, this species has a smoother, narrower and longer cranidium and pygidium, and shallower preglabellar and occipital furrows. It is commonly known as the "slipper trilobite".

species.genus_etymology: aja, from the species name ajax; crepidus, Latin, base. Referring to the species ajax being the base of the
species.species_etymology: ajax, Greek for eagle, the Latin name of the Greek hero Aias, implying vigour like an eagle.
species.synonyms: Arionellus ajax; Lisania ajax; Lisania mirabilis; Ajacicrepida mopanshanensis; Laticeratopyge laevis
species.diagnosis: A small trilobite with smooth dorsal shield. Cranidium gently convex, subtrapezoidal, anterior margin slightly arched forward; dorsal, occipital and anterior border furrows shallow or indistinct; glabella wide and long, gently convex, truncate-conical with broadly rounded front, no glabellar furrows, a small median glabellar node near the occipital furrow posteriorly; occipital ring gently convex, wide medially, narrowing laterally; fixigenae narrow in the palpebral area; palpebral lobes short; preglabellar field extremely narrow or absent; anterior border rather wide, with a small subtriangular posterior spine on the sagittal line; posterior wings longitudinally wide, subtriangular; posterior border furrow extremely shallow. Librigenae rather wide, with medium-length genal spines. Thorax of 9 segments, axis tapering backward; pleural ends with recurved pleural spines, pleural furrows wide and flat. Pygidium extremely short and transversely wide; axis short, of 2 rings, with rounded posterior end; first pair of macropleural ribs extending into a pair of lateral spines; border narrow. With growth, the glabella widens, the glabellar furrows shallower until absent, the anterior border widens, the pygidium becomes shorter and wider, and the lateral pygidial spines lengthen.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Ajacicrepida.

species.synonyms: Hedinaspis sulcata; Hedinaspis (Asiocephalus) sulcata; Hedinaspis tianshanensis
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield elongate-elliptical. Cranidium subtrapezoidal; glabella subcylindrical, with a pit at the centre of the top, with 4 pairs of glabellar furrows not connected to the dorsal furrows: S1 deep and wide, strongly inclined backward, with a glabellar node between them, S2 and S3 pit-like, nearly horizontal; occipital furrow deep and wide laterally; fixigenae with faint reticulate ornament, posterior wings large; eye ridges narrow and convex, nearly horizontal in extension; palpebral lobes small, arcuate; preglabellar field wide, with an inverted-triangular depressed area in front of the glabella; anterior border extremely narrow and convex; anterior branches of facial sutures slightly inclined outward-forward, posterior branches long; librigenae large and wide with slender long genal spines, genal field with distinct radiating reticulate ridges. Thorax of 22 segments, axis convex and extremely narrow; pleural lobes wide and flat, pleural segments horizontal, pleural and interpleural furrows roughly parallel, pleural spines short. Pygidium small, posterior margin often concave medially.
species.remarks: This species has long been regarded as Hedinaspis regalis; the two are very similar, but the latter differs in having a shorter preglabellar field and a smaller, fish-tail-shaped pygidium.

species.diagnosis: Cephalon and pygidium subequal in size, surface smooth. Cranidium subtrapezoidal; glabella cylindrical with rounded front, smooth, without glabellar or occipital furrows; fixigenae about half the glabellar width; anterior border strongly upturned; palpebral lobes convex, about one-third the glabellar length; anterior branches of facial sutures extending slightly outward-forward from the anterior ends of the palpebral lobes, then turning inward, cutting the cranidial margin in an arc; librigenae wide with small genal spines. Thorax of 8 segments; axis narrower than the glabella; pleural lobes flat, anterior pleural spines rather sharp, posterior ones rounded. Pygidium semicircular, about half as long as wide; axis narrow, inverted-conical, with a distinct postaxial ridge; pleural furrows rather shallow; border furrow indistinct; outer margin of the border raised as an arcuate ridge.

species.species_etymology: radiata, radiating, referring to the two pairs of short radiating glabellar furrows of this species
species.diagnosis: Cranidium long-ovate with broadly rounded front; glabella with two pairs of pit-like radiating glabellar furrows; compound eyes of 35-38 rows of polygonal lenses. Thorax of five segments; axis wider than pleurae, gently narrowing backward. Pygidium semi-elliptical; axis short, conical, segmentation faint; pleural lobes indistinctly segmented; border furrow faint on the lateral margins of the pygidium, absent behind the axis.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Xenocyclopyge.

species.species_etymology: Zunyi, Zunyi, Guizhou
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield ovate. Anterior margin of cranidium rounded, without a border; glabella indistinct, without glabellar furrows, with a median node posteriorly; occipital furrow narrow and shallow; occipital ring longitudinally very short; dorsal furrows more distinct behind the palpebral lobes; palpebral lobes medium-sized; posterior wings triangular with a posterior border; librigenae wide with genal spines. Thorax of 8 segments; axis slightly narrower than pleurae; pleural furrows deep, pleural ends rounded. Pygidium semi-elliptical; axis slightly flat; pleural region smooth; no distinct border.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Neopsilocephalina.

species.classification: Order Asaphida / Superfamily Cyclopygoidea / Family Nileidae
species.genus_etymology: Possibly from Latin nilio-, gem
species.species_etymology: armadillo, the species name of the type species of Nileus; -formis, a suffix meaning "shaped like". Indicating the resemblance of this species to the type species.
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield long-ovate, smooth except for fine terrace lines on the articulating facets of the thoracic pleurae and the lateral border of the pygidium. Cephalon semicircular, strongly bent downward forward and anterolaterally; glabella faintly indicated, extremely wide, with a small node at one-third of the posterior length; dorsal furrows extremely shallow; fixigenae narrow and flat in the palpebral area; eyes extremely large and long, crescentic, of several thousand hexagonal lenses; librigenae wider posteriorly with rounded genal angles; anterior branches of facial sutures diverging forward from the eyes, then curving to meet at the front of the dorsal shield; posterior branches short and straight, extending backward-outward to cut the posterior margin; doublure with coarse terrace lines parallel to the anterior margin. Thorax of 8 segments; axis convex and extremely wide; pleural ends rounded, pleural spines absent. Pygidium subsemicircular, axis indistinct, without a posterior border.

Thorax of 8 segments; axis narrower than pleurae; pleural spines absent. Pygidial axis faint, short-conical; pleural region smooth; pygidial border absent.

species.species_etymology: Dali, Dali Village, Jingxi, Guangxi, where abundant fossils of this species occur
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield elongate-elliptical, smooth. Cephalon semicircular; glabella long-cylindrical, slightly constricted in the mid-anterior part; three pairs of glabellar furrows, S1 wide and deep, crossing the glabella and arched backward, S2 shallower, S3 faint; occipital furrow rather wide, slightly arched backward, occipital ring wide; dorsal furrows narrow and deep; palpebral lobes medium-sized, in the mid-posterior part of the cranidium; anterior branches of facial sutures slightly divergent forward, posterior branches oblique backward-outward; fixigenae very narrow; anterior border wide, protruding forward in a triangular shape; librigenae wide with long genal spines. Thorax of 11 segments, axis subequal in width to pleurae; pleural furrows wide and deep, pleural spines short. Pygidium semi-elliptical; axis of three rings plus a terminal piece, extending backward to the border; pleural furrows deep; border narrow.

species.classification: Order Asaphida / Superfamily Remopleuridioidea / Family Hungaiidae
species.genus_etymology: asaphops, Asaphopsis, a trilobite genus name; -oides, resembling, similar to
species.species_etymology: Yongshun, Yongshun County, Hunan, type locality of the type specimens
species.diagnosis: A large trilobite with smooth dorsal shield. Cephalon semi-elliptical; cranidium trapezoidal; glabella weakly convex, conical, with two pairs of glabellar furrows; occipital furrow deep laterally and wide-shallow medially; dorsal furrows forming deep pits on both sides of the front of the glabella; palpebral lobes crescentic, medium-sized, in the mid-posterior part of the glabella; anterior border long and wide-flat; posterior wings transversely extremely long with a spherical end; anterior branches of facial sutures long, meeting on the anterior median line; posterior branches extending nearly horizontally, cutting the posterior border; fixigenae narrow; librigenae wide, tapering anteriorly to meet on the cephalic median line, genal spines slender and long. Thorax of 13 segments; axis narrow, tapering from the 8th segment onward; pleurae straight, interpleural furrows deep, pleural spines sharp. Pygidium elliptical; axis narrow and long, tapering posteriorly with rounded end; pleural region wide with distinct backward-curved pleural segments; border wide and flat, with a pair of small marginal spines laterally.
species.remarks: This species is one of the largest Chinese trilobites, commonly known as the "big pancake". Liu Yiren (1982) recorded the largest individual at 33.5 cm long and 18.4 cm wide.

species.genus_etymology: apat-, Greek, illusion; -kephalus = -cephalus, Greek, head
species.species_etymology: lati, Latin, wide; limbatus, Latin, bordered
species.diagnosis: Axis densely covered with fine nodes; anterior border and cephalic and pygidial doublures with concentric terrace lines. Cephalon subpentagonal with rounded anterior margin, doublure with a ventral median suture; glabella bell-shaped with a long anterior lobe, three pairs of glabellar furrows, S1 deepest, an elongate-elliptical pit extending obliquely inward-backward, S2 nearly parallel to S1, S3 short and shallow; preglabellar field narrow; occipital ring of uniform width; anterior border subtriangular; palpebral lobes large, crescentic; gonatoparian facial sutures; librigenae narrow; border wide; genal spines stout and extremely long. Thorax of 12 segments; axis slightly wider than pleurae, segment 8 with an extremely long axial spine; pleural furrows wide, pleural ends pointed. Pygidium small, sub-elliptical; axis short and stout, of 2 rings plus a terminal piece; 4 pairs of lateral spines arising from the pleural region.

species.genus_etymology: hexac-, hexacanthus, six-spined; -pyge, tail. Referring to the three pairs of pygidial pleural spines of
species.species_etymology: Yichang, Yichang, Hubei, type locality of the type specimens
species.diagnosis: Glabellar terrace lines weak and fine, not easily preserved; median area of the glabella transversely elliptical, anterior tongue with parallel sides or slightly widening forward, strongly bent downward anteriorly, three pairs of very shallow lateral glabellar furrows, expressed as smooth streaks interrupting the terrace-line ornament; anterior border furrow and anterior border both narrow and distinct; eye furrow deep and narrow; palpebral lobes long; eyes large; occipital furrow narrow and deep; occipital ring narrowing laterally, occipital node prominent, very close to the occipital furrow; librigenae very narrow with long, backward-laterally curved genal spines. Thorax of 11 segments; axis about twice the width of the pleurae, some specimens with a long axial spine on segment 8; pleural segments curved backward-laterally with sharp ends. Pygidium small; axis conical; pleural region flat with 3 pairs of pleural ribs, each extended into a pair of pleural spines, the first pair large and the posterior two pairs small.

species.species_etymology: fusiformis, Latin, fusiform, spindle-shaped
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield ovate. species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield ovate, specimens rather small. Three pairs of glabellar furrows; posterior border slightly convex, barely widening laterally, border furrow greatly exaggerated on internal moulds, making the border appear narrower and more convex; palpebral lobes semicircular, opposite L3, distinctly convex; librigenae narrow. Thorax of 9 segments; axial rings subequal in width to the occipital ring. species.species_etymology: In Quechua, the language of the indigenous peoples of the Andes, "amauta" literally means "sage" or "teacher".
species.diagnosis: Cephalon overall subtriangular with a wavy anterior margin; glabella convex, expanding evenly forward, three pairs of glabellar furrows, surface densely covered with nodes of varying size, median lobe with pairs of short spinules; occipital ring with a slightly larger spine and a pair of small lateral spinules; palpebral lobes elevated; eyes composed of 49-52 vertical rows of lenses, 19-21 lenses per row; fixigenae with stout genal spines, with three short spines at the base and the posterior border. Thorax preserved only as fragments, axial rings similar in form to the occipital ring but with possibly 4 axial spines; pleurae with proximal notches on the anterior and posterior margins, similar to the notches on the posterior cephalic margin. Pygidium subtriangular; axis with about 22 rings, rings 1, 5, 9 and 13 with pairs of axial spines; pleural ribs with asymmetric fenestrae and vertical spinules, most fenestrae discontinuous; pygidial mar- gin with a median spine and vertical spinules.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Fenestraspis, and its inter-articular window-like perforations are extremely rare among trilobites. The original literature was not consulted, so the translation of the genus and species names may be inaccurate.

species.species_etymology: Death Valley, Death Valley National Park, California, USA
species.diagnosis: Dorsal shield densely covered with nodes of varying size. Cranidium subtrapezoidal; eyes and palpebral lobes positioned very far back; occipital ring large and raised, with a large occipital node and a pair of short occipital spines on the posterior margin; librigenae wide, lateral border usually with 11 marginal spines, genal spines medium-length. Pygidial axis with two axial rings and a degenerate terminal piece, each ring with a pair of large nodes; five pairs of pygidial pleural spines, the third being a main spine far longer than the others.

Thorax of 10 segments; axis slightly narrower than pleurae; pleurae horizontal, pleural spines rather blunt, those of the last two segments longer. species.species: B. ovata Zhou & Yuan in Zhang et al., 1980
species.species_etymology: ovata, Latin, ovate, possibly referring to the long-ovate dorsal shield
species.diagnosis: A small proparian trilobite with ovate dorsal shield. Glabella slightly constricted forward, cylindrical-conical, slightly constricted medially in the mid-posterior part; palpebral lobes long, close to the glabella. Thorax of 15 segments; the last pair of thor- acic segments almost parallel to the axis. Pygidial axis semicircular, followed by 2 pairs of backward-extending pleural segments and a short V-shaped depression.

species.species: B. multisegmenta Zhao, Yuan & Ahlberg in Yuan et al., 2002
species.species_etymology: multi-, Latin, many; segment, segment. Possibly referring to the greater number of thoracic segments than in the type species
species.diagnosis: This species is rather similar to Burlingia ovata, differing mainly in the wider glabella and thoracic axis, longer palpebral lobes, and 16 thoracic segments. Compared with the type species Burlingia hectori, it has a wider glabella and thoracic axis, longer palpebral lobes, wider librigenae, more thoracic segments, and less curved pleurae.

species.classification: Order Uncertain / Family Burlingiidae
species.genus_etymology: Peng, a surname, in honour of Prof. Peng Shanchi, the first researcher of this genus
species.species_author: Peng Shanchi, Babcock L. E., Lin
species.species_etymology: fusilis, Latin, fused, referring to the completely fused dorsal shield
species.diagnosis: Cranidium, thorax and pygidium completely fused. Glabella conical with pointed-rounded front, 3 pairs of glabellar furrows all disconnected medially, no median node on the glabellar lobes; occipital ring with a median node; preglabellar median ridge absent or faint; palpebral lobes long. Thorax with 9-13 pleural segments, without pleural spines. Pygidium with two backward-extending pleural segments, posterior margin concave.
species.remarks: This species is the type species of the genus Pengia.
